name: Exact Width of Rectangular Filtrations
statement: Let $A_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq A_m$ and $F_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq F_m$ be nonempty classes on disjoint coordinate sets, and put $D_j=\bigcup_{i=0}^j(A_i\times F_i)$. Then $w(D_0,\ldots,D_m)=\max(\{\sigma(A_j):0\leq j\leq m\}\cup\{w(F_0,\ldots,F_m)\})$.
proof: For the upper bound, fill each new inner fiber completely while visiting outer concepts in an optimal order of $A_j$. An old-stage predecessor is replaced inside the current fiber, while a predecessor in an earlier new fiber is replaced at the same inner word using the outer order; the step cost is at most $\max\{\sigma(A_j),\sigma(F_j;F_{j-1})\}$. For the reverse bounds, conditioning $D_j$ at a new inner word recovers $A_j$, and conditioning the pair $(D_j,D_{j-1})$ at any $x\in A_j$ recovers $(F_j,F_{j-1})$.
comments: For one extension, with $\emptyset\ne B\subseteq A$ and $\emptyset\ne F\subsetneq G$, this specializes to $\sigma((A\times F)\cup(B\times G);A\times F)=\max\{\sigma(A),\sigma(B),\sigma(G;F)\}$. If $F=G$, the output is $A\times F$ and the $\sigma(B)$ term is omitted; an empty $B$ likewise reduces to a product.
